meds: metformin, empagliflozin, atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, apixaban, metoprolol

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for prostate cancer treatment decision following two negative biopsies and stable PSA levels.

Long-standing referral for prostate surveillance after initial negative biopsy. The patient is a 68-year-old semi-retired musician living with his partner, with a history of type 2 diabetes managed on metformin and empagliflozin, hypercholesterolaemia on atorvastatin and rosuvastatin, and atrial fibrillation treated with apixaban and metoprolol. He smokes 17 pack-years and consumes 7 units of alcohol weekly. Gardening is his primary physical activity, and he reports no structured exercise. PSA has remained stable at 0.5 ng/mL since April 2022, with the most recent value 0.44 ng/mL. Cardiology review in autumn 2024 confirmed stable atrial fibrillation management. He declined participation in research trials previously.

Per rectum, the prostate is non-palpable with no nodularity or asymmetry, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished man with stable vital signs, BMI 27.4, and no signs of acute distress or lymphadenopathy.
